Question
========

The command `f <- factor(30:32)` creates a factor with levels `"30", "31", "32"`. What will the expression `f - 10`
return?

Choose the answer with the most appropriate justification.

Answerlist
----------

* `NA, NA, NA`, because arithmetic on factors isn't well-defined, so there is no unambiguous solution.
* `NA`, because arithmetic on factors isn't well-defined, so there is no unambiguous solution.
* `NA, NA, NA`, because factor level names are character vectors, and arithmetic on character vectors isn't well-defined.
* `20, 21, 22`, because R converts the factor levels to numeric values before doing any arithmetic.
* `"20", "21", "22"`, because R first computes the difference and then converts answer to a character vector.
* `-9, -8, -7`, because R converts the factor levels to numeric values before doing any arithmetic.
* `"30", "31", "32"`, because R returns `f` unchanged, since arithmetic with factors is not well-defined.
* The expression will return an error, because R refuses to do arithmetic with factors.

Solution
========

Even though this factor's level *names* happen to look like numbers, arithmetic on a factor simply isn't possible. R
doesn't know how to implement the calculation we've requested, so every element of the result becomes a missing value,
`NA`. A missing value is a datum for which we don't know the true value. In this case, R uses the missing values to say,
"I don't have enough information to say what the answer should be."
